title: Quote the price tag
prompt:
The shop page needs a tagline file. In Mira’s home directory, create `tagline.txt` holding exactly this one line, dollar sign and double quotes included:

```
Pixel Raiders costs $5 for "early birds"
```

Use `echo` and a redirection, and check the file with `cat tagline.txt`.
hints: `echo text > tagline.txt` writes a line into a file, replacing what was there.
Inside double quotes the shell still expands `$5` (to nothing) and the inner double quotes end the string early.
Single quotes keep everything inside them exactly as typed, so they protect both the `$` and the `"`.
solution: echo 'Pixel Raiders costs $5 for "early birds"' > tagline.txt
check:
if [ ! -e tagline.txt ]; then no "There is no tagline.txt yet. Create it in Mira’s home directory."; exit 1; fi
ok "tagline.txt exists."
want='Pixel Raiders costs $5 for "early birds"'
got=$(cat tagline.txt)
if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then ok "It holds the line exactly, with the dollar sign and the double quotes."
else no "It holds “$(head -c 200 tagline.txt)”. Compare it with the line asked for: a dollar sign or quotes went missing."; fi

title: A variable in every new shell
prompt:
Mira’s build scripts read the studio’s name from the environment variable `STUDIO`. Set it up so that `STUDIO` has the value `TuxPixel` in every new shell Mira opens, and in the programs those shells start.

Then try it: open a new shell with `bash` and run `echo $STUDIO`, then leave that shell with `exit`.
hints: Bash reads `~/.bashrc` each time it starts an interactive shell, so a line added there runs in every new shell.
A plain `STUDIO=TuxPixel` stays inside the shell; `export` passes the variable on to the programs the shell starts.
Append a line with `>>`, which adds to the end of a file instead of replacing it (`>` would wipe `.bashrc`).
check:
v=$(runuser -u mira -- env -i HOME=/home/mira TERM=dumb bash -i -c 'printf %s "$STUDIO"' < /dev/null 2> /dev/null)
if [ "$v" = TuxPixel ]; then ok "A new shell has STUDIO=TuxPixel."
else no "A new interactive shell doesn’t have STUDIO=TuxPixel (it has “$v”). Add a line to ~/.bashrc."; exit 1; fi
c=$(runuser -u mira -- env -i HOME=/home/mira TERM=dumb bash -i -c 'bash -c "printf %s \"\$STUDIO\""' < /dev/null 2> /dev/null)
if [ "$c" = TuxPixel ]; then ok "Programs the shell starts see it too: it is exported."
else no "Programs started from the shell don’t see STUDIO: the variable is set but not exported."; fi
if [ "$(wc -l < .bashrc)" -gt 20 ]; then ok "The rest of .bashrc is still there."
else no "Most of .bashrc is gone. Did you use > instead of >>? Start over and append with >>."; fi
